synopsis: OpenSCENARIO is part of the booklet’s recommended scenario catalogue and integration infrastructure, alongside OpenDRIVE and OSI; usable simulation also requires validated sensor, dynamics and friction models, site models and calibration datasets [f913, f8335, f15862]. It describes actor movement over time: XML version 1.4.0, dated 2026, supports precise synchronized maneuvers, while DSL version 2.2.0, dated March 2026, explicitly represents abstract scenarios, parameter ranges and performance indicators [f13204, f13205]. Both forms retain a road-traffic domain model, and no study was found from the listed industry and standards organizations on applying OpenSCENARIO, ISO 34502 or the UNECE New Assessment/Test Method to off-road machines [f13206, f1698]. The booklet therefore recommends OpenDRIVE only for structured haul roads, OpenUSD and OpenMATERIAL for scenes, and OpenSCENARIO export where tools require it [f13216]. Vendor support includes MathWorks, Prescan and MORAI—the latter listing OpenSCENARIO 1.x—and VTD 2025.2 added a native ScenarioEngine on 1 October 2025; compatibility establishes data exchange, not physical fidelity [f8383, f8458, f8512, f8429, f8921]. Procurement should require OpenSCENARIO, OSI, FMI and OpenUSD exports, with ownership-change exit clauses to mitigate supplier dependence [f16487, f8887].
